body:
Documents-mode sanitization now preserves durations, JSON stack frames and empty profile fields while detecting the document variants and personal URL paths reported in #87–#88. Repeated label-pattern construction is removed; the remaining structured JSON cost is measured and documented under #86's explicit alternative acceptance criterion.

Fixes #86
Fixes #87
Fixes #88
Fixes #89

## Changes

- Require affirmative personal-age context. Keep all nine reported durations and ambiguous bare `34 года`; retain ages after `мне`, `возраст`, `исполнилось` and gender context.
- Prevent the escaped `n` in JSON `\n` from becoming an obfuscated-email local part. Preserve both complete reported stacks, including line breaks and frame names.
- Preserve `Гражданство: не указано` and `Дети: нет`, while retaining meaningful disability/criminal-record negatives as sensitive.
- Redact `/u/<name>` and `/in/<name>` under `url`, alongside existing personal path families. Preserve operational `0.0.0.0` bind addresses with explicit private-policy overrides intact.
- Implement every #88 variant: phone/messenger/obfuscated-email labels, passport issuer and account abbreviations, titles and arbitrary-ending Cyrillic surnames with two initials, birth years, age/gender forms, citizenship/children/residence phrases and English employer/company/education labels. None of those reported forms is deferred as a limit.
- Precompile immutable personal-label regexes and avoid redundant explicit clones where `matchAll` isolates iteration. Keep all structured standalone scans, native detection and external-engine views.
- Add the patch changeset required by the automated release process.

## Requirements, alternatives and performance

The [complete requirement inventory and research](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-89-9faef95b7b9a/docs/case-studies/issue-89/README.md) maps every requirement and reported row to implementation and tests. It evaluates Presidio, libphonenumber-js and fast-redact and explains why existing bounded rules fit this patch without new dependencies. All required issue bodies/comments/sub-issues and all three PR feedback endpoints were inspected; there was no additional feedback or nested required scope. None of the three issues was wholly resolved at baseline.

The [coverage guide](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-89-9faef95b7b9a/docs/COVERAGE.md#structured-json-cost-issue-86) documents per-call measurements and main-thread implications. On this Linux x64 Node 26 container, median milliseconds per sanitize call were:

| JSON fixture | 0.16.0 | 0.16.1 | This change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 89 characters | 1.21 | 8.44 | 4.67 |
| Exact reported 264-character fixture | 1.81 | 19.71 | 11.15 |
| 9,396 characters | 10.04 | 37.88 | 28.32 |

**Remaining overhead exceeds 2x of 0.16.0.** #86 explicitly accepts documented higher cost; this PR meets that alternative, without removing the 0.16.1 string-boundary detection. Only the 264-character source payload was supplied; the short/9 KiB fixtures approximate the other reported lengths. These are local measurements, not universal timing guarantees. Existing detection changes only where #87 clarifies false positives and #88 adds coverage.

## Reproduction and verification

- Reproduce all reported document cases with `node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-issue-89.test.js`.
- Reproduce the stack bug with `sanitize(JSON.stringify({stack: 'Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:5432\n    at TCPConnectWrap.afterConnect (node:net:1595:16)'}), {profile: 'documents', structured: 'json'})`: the original `\n` and frame are now preserved.
- New suite: **195 passing tests**, covering text/JSON/JSONL, payload removal, exact placeholder restoration, asynchronous parity, all path families, private bind-address overrides and isolated regex iteration.
- The same suite against archived 0.16.1 reports **119 failures and 76 passes**, reproducing the original bugs using `node experiments/issue-89/test-baseline.mjs /path/to/0.16.1/src/index.js`.
- Focused existing compatibility run: **227 passing tests** across issue #84, document entities, context, escape integrity and structured handling. The obsolete bare-age expectation from #82 is updated to #87's clarified policy.
- Reproduce finite serial timing comparisons with `node --max-old-space-size=256 experiments/issue-89/benchmark.mjs [released-src/index.js]`.
- Changed-file ESLint/Prettier and changeset validation pass. **All current-head CI workflows pass** at `70dbb62948cf2b237c1a1fe3c734c45690a8eb23`: 40 successful checks, 10 intentional skips, no failures. [Runtime/platform matrix and pipeline](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42058619309), [example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42058619339), [security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42058619305) and [links](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42058619669). Node, Bun and Deno tests pass on Linux, Windows and macOS.
- No UI changes; screenshots do not apply.

body:
Structured JSON/JSONL values now receive the same line-start detection as plain text, including CV employers in arrays and embedded JSON. The documents profile also covers the contact, identity, name, attribute, employer, school and residence forms reported in #78–#83.

Fixes #77
Fixes #78
Fixes #79
Fixes #80
Fixes #81
Fixes #82
Fixes #83
Fixes #84

## Changes

- Share decoded, source-mapped string views between synchronous inspection and the asynchronous engine union. Preserve JSON escapes, identifier keys, structural-field policy and safe bytes; bound embedded JSON container traversal to two layers.
- Protect the reported Russian mobile formats, obfuscated emails, messenger/profile links, passport series/numbers, other identity/payment numbers, initial/inflected names, birth years, age/gender and labelled profile attributes.
- Extend synonymous employer, school and residence labels, numbered schools and structural street addresses. All five partial-redaction examples in #80 now lose their identifying digits.
- Preserve operational relative `url` values and ISO-style `time` timestamps. Treat context-free 40-hex values consistently as ambiguous SHA-1-shaped identifiers; credential context, known secrets, provider rules and external engines still apply.
- Add a patch changeset and default-off structured-value count tracing.

## Explicit coverage decisions

The issue acceptance criteria permit documented limits for ambiguous forms. `Спасибо, Анна!`, `Анна, добрый день!`, `Менеджер Анна` and `Лютик, менеджер` remain unchanged without additional context/known values. Salary is outside the native document rules (`зарплата 150 000 руб.`, `Salary: 150000`). These are documented and tested, with no follow-up implementation deferred. Standalone public addresses can resemble personal addresses; the ordinary public-place prose negative stays unchanged. Social account paths cannot distinguish people from organization accounts. Bare 40-hex secrets require known values or credential context.

None of the seven issues was wholly resolved at the baseline. Every issue body, comment list, native sub-issue and PR feedback endpoint was inspected; no additional required sub-issues or feedback were present.

## Reproduction, requirements and alternatives

Run `node experiments/issue-84/compare.mjs [absolute-path-to-other-src/index.js]` for all 128 original text-table rows. For example, `sanitize(JSON.stringify({note: 'Менеджер, Ромашка (2019 – 2021)'}), {profile: 'documents', structured: 'json'})` now removes the employer.

The [complete requirement inventory](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-84-7c4f150def22/docs/case-studies/issue-84/README.md) records every table row, implementation choice, root causes and primary-source research into Presidio, Natasha, libphonenumber-js, Git hashes and Internet timestamps. No new dependency or model download is needed. [Coverage policy and limits](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-84-7c4f150def22/docs/COVERAGE.md) document all decisions.

## Verification

- Baseline reproduction: running the actual new suite against archived 0.16.0 source produces 116 failures and 43 passes (`experiments/issue-84/test-baseline.mjs`).
- New `tests/sanitizer-issue-84.test.js`: 159 passing cases covering source rows, complete numeric removal, ordinary prose, JSON/JSONL, nested JSON, escaped offsets/restoration, unsafe URLs and asynchronous/custom engine anchors.
- Combined issue #84 and reused-map regression run: 196 passing cases, including independent tokens for newly recognized lowercase full names and exact restoration.
- Focused compatibility checks passed for existing document entities, CV experience lines, contexts, escape integrity, JSONL record workers, issue #34/#65 and placeholder escaping. Full runtime/platform suites run in CI.
- Bounded adversarial probes use finite 4–5 KiB inputs and a 256 MiB JS heap; no unexpected findings or hangs.
- No frontend changes; screenshots are not applicable.

Final validation on `95eac89bf6ae797fc3257c173f381b6ada9bdcfd`: **40 checks succeeded, 10 jobs skipped by workflow conditions, no failures or pending checks**.

- [Checks and release: full Node/Bun/Deno matrix on Linux, Windows and macOS](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42046882423)
- [Example app: web build and desktop packages on all three platforms](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42046882199)
- [Security checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42046882189)
- [Documentation link checks](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/42046882968)

Transient HTTP 504 errors during Electron/Deno downloads passed on rerun. The original CI failures and baseline evidence are preserved locally in `ci-logs/` and summarized in the case study. The latest default branch is an ancestor of this branch; the working tree is clean. This PR remains unmerged.

body:
## Summary

Solves #73 and #74, as #75 asks, in one pull request. Neither was already resolved: every failing row in both issues reproduced on `0.15.0` before the change.

Fixes #73
Fixes #74
Fixes #75

### #73: reused map parts

A reused map PERSON entry now matches the same forms as an explicit `knownPersonal` value. Measured with `experiments/issue-75/compare-73.mjs` on a map seeded by `Кандидат: Петров Данил.`:

| Input                                     | `0.15.0`                               | This pull request                          |
| ----------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------ |
| `Опыт: петров день, данил, мария.`        | `Опыт: Person-1 день, данил, мария.`   | unchanged input                            |
| `Навыки: Битрикс петров, Excel.`          | `Навыки: Битрикс Person-1, Excel.`     | unchanged input                            |
| `Навыки: Роман петров (CRM), отдел.`      | `Навыки: Роман Person-1 (CRM), отдел.` | unchanged input                            |
| `Опыт.\nСтек: Максим петрова (ПМ), отдел.` | `ERR_RESIDUAL`                         | unchanged input                            |
| `Отзыв: Алина петрову, отдел.`            | `ERR_RESIDUAL`                         | unchanged input                            |
| `Петров пришёл.`                          | `Person-1 пришёл.`                     | unchanged input                            |
| `Позвонили Петрову Данилу.`               | `Позвонили Person-1.`                  | `Позвонили Person-1.`                      |
| `Д. Петров пришёл.`                       | `Person-1 пришёл.`                     | `Person-1 пришёл.`                         |
| `петров данил пришёл.`                    | `Person-1 пришёл.`                     | `Person-1 пришёл.`                         |

Root cause: three paths treated a stored value as evidence about the next document. Bare `-ов`/`-ев` patterns were built from stored values (which is why `петров` matched and `мороз` did not), `related` linked a word to any part of a stored alias, and `placeholderReplacement` then recorded the bare surface as a new value, polluting saved maps.

- Bare patterns and the part rule now need evidence from the current document, its stream batches or its decoded values.
- A single capitalized stored word no longer matches lower-case text.
- A part listed in `knownPersonal` stays matchable alone through a new optional `standalone` entry field, which is validated and survives JSON and Lino serialization.
- A matching bare part covers the adjacent given name or patronymic through `coverAdjacentNames`, placeholder mode only.
- The #67–#70 suites pass unchanged.

### #74: labelled experience lines

```
Опыт: Менеджер по продажам, [ORGANIZATION_1] (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01)
Должность: Менеджер | Опыт: Аналитик, [ORGANIZATION_1] (2018-01-01 — 2020-12-01)
Менеджер, [ORGANIZATION_1] (2018-01 – по н.в.)
```

- A label of one or two words before the title is read like a list marker, with `:`, ` - ` or ` — `. A segment after `|` is read like a line start.
- Titles reach nine words, and `по н.в.` and `по н/в` end a range.
- The date range stays the anchor: `Итог: Встреча, понедельник (2019-05-01 — 2021-03-01) перенесена.` stays unchanged, as does the rest of the prose table.
- The default profile ignores these lines, and hostile lines stay linear: 8000 repeated dates took about 241 ms both before and after the change.

## Behavior to review

- **In-document propagation is unchanged.** The issue's reference is the fresh-map result, so `Кандидат: Петров Данил. Опыт: петров день.` still gives `Person-1 день`. Tightening it would change fresh-map output and could add under-redaction.
- **Legacy maps.** Bare surfaces recorded by 0.14 and 0.15 are ignored on reuse when they are part of a longer value in the same entry. Such a map cannot tell a listed part from a recorded one, so a listed part must be listed again in `knownPersonal` to match alone.

## Limits

- **The private 175-CV corpus could not be re-measured**, so the reported 14 shared-map refusals are verified only through the reproductions in the issue, not as a corpus count.
- A given name outside the bounded list stays next to the placeholder when a stored bare part matches.
- `Позже Петров` is still one `name-identity` span with fresh and reused maps alike. This predates the change.

## Existing components

None was adopted. LangChain's reversible Presidio anonymizer, Natasha and pyresparser are Python pipelines, and this package is a JavaScript library with finite rules. Sources and reasoning are in `docs/case-studies/issues-73-74/README.md`, with one row per requirement mapped to its verification.

## Verification

- `node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/*.test.js`: 1744 tests, 1744 pass. CI passes on Node, Bun and Deno across Ubuntu, macOS and Windows.
- New `tests/sanitizer-reused-map-parts.test.js` covers issue rows, a polluted legacy map, JSON records, streams, async and serialization. `tests/sanitizer-experience-lines.test.js` gains the label table and hostile timing.
- Reproduce with `node experiments/issue-75/compare-73.mjs [path-to-another-src-index.js]` and `node experiments/issue-75/lines-74.mjs`.
title: fix: Match reused map parts like known values and read labelled experience lines

body:
## Summary

Solves all four open issues in one pull request. None of them was already resolved: every failing row reported in #67–#70 reproduced on the base commit with `experiments/issue-71/reproduce.mjs` and now gives the expected result.

Fixes #67
Fixes #68
Fixes #69
Fixes #70
Fixes #71

### #67: known Russian name forms

- Known names now match in all six cases, including `-ичем`, and in both word orders.
- Surname + given name of a three-part value, `ё`/`е` in both directions, and initials (`Петров Д. С.`, `Д. С. Петров`, `Петрову Д. С.`) also match. All forms map to one entity and restore exactly.
- A bare surname or given name stays unmatched unless listed, because it is ambiguous. `docs/API.md` and `README.md` now say to list each part you want matched on its own.

### #68: one fake identity

```
Петров пришёл. Позвонили Петрову. Нет Петрова. С Петровым.
Баранов пришёл. Позвонили Баранову. Нет Баранова. С Барановым.

Работал в ООО «Ромашка», затем снова в Ромашке.
Работал в ООО «Импульс», затем снова в Импульсе.
```

- All forms of a known person, organization, school or location get one fake that keeps gender and word order and takes the case of the matched form.
- `Example Organization N` is replaced by authored Russian and Latin vocabularies.
- New hook: `transformation.pools`. It is not the `fakeValues` map floated in #68, because `fakeValues` is already an array of identity values to retain.

### #69: residuals

- `@handle/email` now gives `Username-1/Email-1`.
- `Вектор-99` is one span, and later numbered mentions are replaced in the `documents` profile.
- A placeholder followed by a digit now fails with `ERR_RESIDUAL`.
- With a shared map, numbered and bare names no longer fail or produce tokens like `Organization-199`.

### #70: CV experience lines

The `documents` profile detects employers anchored on a date range at confidence 0.60, including quoted names, and propagates them. All eight table rows produce the expected output and restore exactly. The rule does not run in the default profile.

## Behavior changes to review

- Fake organizations, schools and locations no longer read as visibly synthetic, as #68 asked. They can coincide with real entities that the text does not mention.
- Entity names are tracked per transformation object so that two entities never share a name. A name can therefore depend on first appearance when two entities collide, and this state is not shared across worker threads. This is documented in `docs/API.md`.

## Limitations

- **Corpus not re-measured:** the 236-document corpus from #69 and #70 is private, so the aggregate numbers were not re-measured and the actual miss rate after this change is unknown. Tests cover the published rows and shapes.
- **Other types in #70:** the EDUCATION, PERSON and LOCATION miss counts have no published shapes or acceptance rows, so those types were not changed.
- **Prepositions:** a source preposition stays as written (`о Осипове`, `со Потаповой`). Changing it would touch text outside the finding.
- **Experience lines not targeted:** `Title, Employer, City (dates)` and titles containing a comma can leave the employer in place. Date-anchored prose of the same shape can be flagged.
- **Autodetected names in fake mode:** mentions that occur only in oblique forms stay separate entities, as in placeholder mode. Listed `knownPersonal` values do not have this limitation.
- **Transliterated known values:** a Latin spelling of a known Cyrillic name is still not matched under `knownOnly`. No issue requires it.

## Verification

- Regression tests: `tests/sanitizer-known-forms.test.js`, `tests/sanitizer-fake-identity.test.js`, `tests/sanitizer-placeholder-residual.test.js`, `tests/sanitizer-experience-lines.test.js`. The last includes a timing test on hostile lines.
- Reproduce with `node experiments/issue-71/reproduce.mjs`.
- Local sanitizer suite: 1127 passed, 0 failed. Lint, formatting, duplication and line-limit checks passed. The full matrix runs in CI.

Requirements, research and alternatives are in [the case study](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-71-63a050a5595f/docs/case-studies/issue-71/README.md). A release changeset is included.

body:
Russian CV entities and inflected known values could leak through sanitization, fake names could misclassify given names, and technical prose could trigger placeholder collisions or credential redactions. This PR fixes all seven issues in #65 and adds reversible known-only sanitization.

- **#58:** Reserve actual placeholder labels with Unicode boundaries. GPT-4, ISO-9001 and Windows-10 remain unchanged and restore exactly; actual namespace/map collisions still fail.
- **#59:** Extend the opt-in documents profile for quoted employers, organization cores across documents/streams, group markers, Russian institutions/acronyms, residence/city forms and introduction/sign-off names.
- **#60 and #64:** Match whole Unicode words with bounded Russian case forms, reordered names and organization cores for known values and restore-map identities. Store each original surface for exact restoration.
- **#61:** Constrain credential labels and verbal values, preserve source references and prose, retain real-secret detection, and report `irreversibleRedactions` for placeholder replacements absent from the map.
- **#62:** Infer Russian given-name roles and gender from surname/patronymic context and replace complete person spans.
- **#63:** Add `knownOnly: true` and CLI `--known-only` across sync/async, structured, stream, fake and placeholder paths. Automatic detectors, including credentials, are disabled; explicit `knownSecrets` remain supported. Keep existing `redact()` return types compatible.
- Include API/coverage documentation and a minor-release changeset.

The [requirement inventory and research](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-65-41acbb882c38/docs/case-studies/issue-65/README.md) maps every issue to implementation and verification. Existing Faker supplies localized names; bounded offline matching avoids new runtime dependencies. Optional `personalFields` inference is unnecessary for the chosen known-value API: callers supply `knownPersonal` explicitly. Morphology remains bounded to known/confirmed identities, and document detection remains opt-in.

CI fix: the failed ARM64 macOS jobs executed zero steps and reported hosted-runner acquisition failures and ARM64 capacity constraints. Fresh gate logs report `Failing jobs: test` (release gate, line 264) and `Failing jobs: desktop-package` (example gate, line 215). Both workflows now use the [supported `macos-26-intel` pool](https://github.blog/changelog/2026-02-26-macos-26-is-now-generally-available-for-github-hosted-runners/) for native macOS x64 runtime checks, desktop packaging and opt-in iOS builds. Electron explicitly targets ARM64 to preserve the Apple Silicon artifact. All nine OS/runtime combinations and both mandatory pipeline gates remain enabled. When Intel execution exposed actual timeouts, the two large streaming fixtures retained their >7 MiB/>10 MiB input-size and credential assertions with simpler padding; JSONL also checks exact ordinary-field preservation. macOS tests now run in three deterministic groups per runtime, with every file included exactly once. Existing 30-second Node/Bun test limits and 300/200/100-second suite budgets are unchanged. Shard selection and runtime arguments have automated regression coverage. Further Bun deadlines were traced to repeated scans of long padding and an unnecessarily million-character synthetic credential. Native keyword/ASCII fast paths reduce padding work; the oversized-record regression still checks a complete 4,096-character credential beyond its initial scan window, while a bounded experiment retains the original extreme case. Windows Bun remained slow on the large JSON string value. The final limit/transport fixture uses valid JSON whitespace for its >7 MiB padding, retaining both oversized records, automatic password detection and exact output-field preservation; the original large string-value workload remains in a bounded experiment. The change applies to PRs and main; no manual repository action or missing-secret exception is required.

Validation:

- Reproduce and verify the reported product cases with `node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-issue-65.test.js`: all 75 regression checks pass. The initial 72-check draft failed 59 checks against default-branch commit `ee7b51c`, across all seven issue groups.
- Focused validation: 120 product/workflow/pipeline checks passed, followed by 101 checks for shard completeness, execution budgets, large streams and all 75 issue regressions. A further 42 policy checks pass after updating the concurrency assertion to require distinct shard keys. Changed-file lint/formatting and workflow policy validation pass.
- Focused compatibility checks from implementation passed for credential formats/context, earlier regressions, placeholders, CLI, escaping, documents and fake values. CI runs the full platform/runtime suites (15 jobs covering nine OS/runtime combinations).
- Latest focused verification: 201 Node checks and 100 Bun checks pass, including Unicode/representation compatibility, all product regressions, large Gitleaks records and JSONL streams. Bun completes the Gitleaks case in 0.69 seconds and the final JSONL transport case in 5.3 seconds under the unchanged 30-second limit.
- The final JSONL change also passes all 81 Node checks covering JSONL streams and the complete issue regression suite; pre-commit lint/formatting pass.
- **Current head `45093c7`: all five workflows and every required check pass**, including all 15 runtime jobs and both previously failing Pipeline Status gates: [Checks and release](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/41881135181), [Example app](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/41881135120), [Security](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/41881135189), [Workflows](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/41881135308), [Broken Link Checker](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/actions/runs/41881135226). Linux Bun passes all 1,630 tests and Windows Bun passes all 1,593; the formerly failing JSONL test takes 3.1 seconds and 2.68 seconds respectively, under the unchanged 30-second limit.
- Latest `main` (`ee7b51c`) is included. Full PR diff reviewed for requirements, compatibility and preserved features.

body:
Documents can now use readable, reusable `Person-1`, `Organization-1`, `Education-1`, `Location-1`, `Email-1`, `Phone-1` and `Date-1` placeholders, restore original text from a private map, and opt into employer/school/location detection without preceding context words.

- **#54:** shared per-type counters, configurable collision-checked token formats, alias-aware name linking, cross-file map reuse, exact free-text/JSON/JSONL restoration, derived-response restoration, JSON and Links Notation serialization, API/CLI map handling and restore commands. Maps use atomic `0600` writes, stay separate from sanitized output and are rejected as publication inputs. Credentials stay redacted and excluded unless explicitly opted in. `map: false` discards the temporary registry and still checks residuals.
- **#55:** opt-in `documents` profile / `documentEntities` rules for legal-form organizations in either order, educational institution type words, a bounded offline city/region vocabulary and location labels. Explicit confidence scores, all 17 locale fixtures, public exemptions/private overrides, and placeholder/fake support. Existing profiles keep their default detector behavior.
- Apply the behavior across sync/async, structured keys and values, CLI, ordered JSONL streams and bounded file APIs. Include public types, a runnable example, safety/coverage documentation and a minor release changeset.

The [complete requirements and solution plan](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-56-4276380c7297/experiments/issue-56/PLAN.md) maps every parent/sub-issue requirement to implementation and verification. The [investigation](https://github.com/link-foundation/sensitive-data-sanitizer/blob/issue-56-4276380c7297/docs/case-studies/issue-56-placeholders/README.md) records root causes, alternatives and primary-source research on Links Notation, Presidio, compromise and GeoNames. Both missing features reproduced before implementation; neither issue is deferred or classified as already resolved.

Reproduction and verification:

- Before: `sanitize('Jane Doe', {transformation: {mode: 'placeholder'}})` throws `ERR_CONFIG`; the issue's list-form CV examples yield no document findings. Run `node experiments/issue-56/reproduce.mjs` for the examples and fixed document-profile output.
- After: `Jane Doe met J. Doe` becomes `Person-1 met Person-1`; `restore(result.text, result.map)` restores the exact original surfaces. Reusing a map preserves identities and continues counters. `redact cv.txt --profile documents --placeholder --map private.lino --output safe.txt` writes private mapping separately; `restore safe.txt --map private.lino` restores it.
- New automated suites: `tests/sanitizer-placeholders.test.js`, `tests/sanitizer-document-entities.test.js`, `tests/sanitizer-placeholder-cli.test.js`, and `tests/sanitizer-placeholder-escaping.test.js`. Cover all 17 locales, escaped keys/values, both serializations, collisions, variants, credentials, residual failure, map permissions/publication rejection, file reuse, mixed encoded/plain source ordering and exact multi-batch stream restoration. Bounded adversarial JSON tests cover the linear scanner introduced after CodeQL review.
- Focused local validation: all 55 new checks pass in Node, Bun and Deno. The six package metadata tests, 85 adjacent transformation/fake/credential/JSONL tests, and 21 public-policy/JSON/residual checks pass. Deno follows the existing permission-gated filesystem test convention; Node and Bun exercise private file writes and CLI restoration. title: feat: Unify tool-log sanitization and remove large-input bottlenecks

body:
Fixes #38.

Credential-label spans no longer block session publication. Prose such as `token for ES.`, `SIG for\n:sig is d` and `token for\\ery record … request-log write lock` stays unchanged. A quoted `sig:'` value never reaches the following JSON keys. `APIkey="\"private_key:9"` is published as `APIkey="[REDACTED]"`.

- **Label boundaries:** credential qualifiers (`for/от/для/…`) stay on one logical line. They cannot cross escaped `\n`, escape sequences or quotes. Verbs such as `is/es/est` are whole words, so `request` no longer ends in the verb `est`.
- **Generic labels in prose:** `token`, `sig`, `secret`, `cookie` and similar labels followed by a verb need a generated-looking value. Password-family and compound labels (`the password is hunter2`, `api key is …`) are unchanged.
- **Values never include JSON keys:** quoted values are bounded by the enclosing JSON string, including strings at the start of a structured batch line.
- **Same encoding layer:** a credential covering a whole escaped JSON run is redacted as one value, instead of re-encoding a sanitized copy that lost its label. Base64 payloads under `preserveEncoding` are still re-encoded.
- **Fixed-point re-redaction:** when verification still finds a value, the output is redacted again for up to three rounds (`residualRounds`). Each round emits a value-free `residual-redaction` debug event. Output that does not converge still fails with `ERR_RESIDUAL`, and structured JSON verification still runs on the final text. The sync and async paths share `redactAgain`.
- **Corpus, docs, release:** the issue records are added to the Codex/Claude publication corpus. The PR also adds a patch Changeset, API documentation, a case study (`docs/case-studies/issue-38-credential-labels/README.md`), and experiments in `experiments/issue-38/`.

### Reproduction

```sh
node experiments/issue-38/reproduce.mjs          # main: ERR_JSON_COLLISION + 4× ERR_RESIDUAL
node experiments/issue-38/fuzz.mjs 3000 1         # main: 23/3000 blocked (19 collision, 4 residual)
node --test --test-timeout=30000 tests/sanitizer-issue-38.test.js   # main: 28/36 fail
node --max-old-space-size=512 experiments/issue-34/session-corpus.mjs  # main: ERR_JSON_COLLISION
```

### Tests

`tests/sanitizer-issue-38.test.js` has 36 tests:
- Every issue record goes through `sanitize`, `createSanitizer().sanitize`, `sanitizeJsonl`, and `sanitizeStreamToFile` with `twoPass` false and true.
- Prose label boundaries must stay unchanged.
- Credential values must still be redacted in plain and JSONL text, with keys preserved.
- Fixed-point redaction is checked in the sync and async engines, and a non-converging detector must still fail closed.

One existing expectation changed. `sanitizer-stream-identity.test.js` ("never reuses coordinator findings for residual verification") now expects the fresh verifier's late finding to be redacted rather than raise `ERR_RESIDUAL`. Its detector also returns no finding once the value is gone. This matches the issue's request for fixed-point re-redaction.

### Validation

- Node 1,355 / 1,355, Bun 1,355 / 1,355, Deno 1,210 + 8 steps.
- `npm run check` (lint, format, duplication) and the file line limits pass.
- The extended session corpus has zero residuals with 1 and 4 workers.
- Fuzz: 0 failures with seeds 1, 7 and 99 at 8,000 records each, and no residual rounds were needed.

### Assumptions and limits

- The private 911-session corpus was not supplied, so these results give no new pass rate for it.
- A short dictionary word after a generic label and a verb (`the token is valid`) is treated as text. Use `knownSecrets` to redact such a value when it really is a credential.
